title: Ingest asks tasklist before every extracted frame: the Resolve probe costs 2.7x the frames it guards
what: _should_stop() re-runs the full gate before every stage and before every one-frame seek in _make_frames. In the default idle run mode with the editor away, the gate reaches _resolve_running() = resolve_prefs.resolve_is_running(), an uncached tasklist spawn (proxy_gen caches the same probe for 60 s). broll_ingest_skip_while_resolve defaults to True; music inherits the same path.
cost: ~29 tasklist spawns per 90 s clip (frames every <=4 s plus stage checks). Measured: 23 tasklist calls 5.4 s vs the 23 frame seeks 1.96 s. 400 clips of 60 s ~8,000 spawns (~30 min wall); 2,000-clip batch ~40,000 spawns (1.8-2.6 h).
evidence: Code read; tasklist timed at 0.16 s (10 calls) and 0.235 s (23 calls under load); frames_probe.py on a synthetic 90 s 1080p h264 clip.
ledger: new (MED-9 2026-08-11 fixed the same pattern in proxy_gen only)
fix: TTL-cache (5-15 s) the Resolve probe for the between-stage/between-frame _should_stop, keep the fresh probe for the tick gate, keep fail-closed. Secondary: one select= ffmpeg pass beat 23 seeks (0.64 s vs 1.96 s) on a 90 s clip; use only below a duration threshold.

title: The ingest state file is re-serialised whole, pretty-printed, at every stage of every item: O(n^2) bytes per batch
what: Every checkpoint deep-copies and rewrites the whole batch plus every retained staging drop (7-day retention) with the pure-Python indent=2 encoder under the GIL. One item passes ~12 saves, so bytes written grow as ~12 n x size(n).
cost: Measured per save: 400 items 15.7 ms / 1.35 MB; 2,000 items 84 ms / 6.75 MB. 400-clip card ~4,800 saves = ~6.5 GB written, ~75 s CPU; 2,000-clip card (server MAX_BATCH_ITEMS) ~24,000 saves = ~160 GB written, ~34 min CPU (totals estimated from measured per-save cost).
evidence: save_probe.py: synthetic snapshot shaped like _save's; compact separators 6.2-6.8x faster and 31% smaller.
ledger: new (comp-broll-music-1 2026-09-03 fixed thread safety, not cost)
fix: (a) separators=(',', ':'); (b) dirty flag flushed at most every 2-5 s from the tick, synchronous only at transitions a restart cannot rediscover (claim, lease change, held-for-base-rig, batch end). Crunch steps re-derive done-ness from artifacts on disk, so a lost checkpoint costs a re-run stage, never a wrong one. Keep per-thread tmp + _save_lock.

title: The music page's 30 s Resolve-status poll re-launches the onefile companion exe every time, even with Resolve closed and the tab hidden
what: Each /music/status is subprocess.run of the frozen companion re-entered with --music-resolve-worker: onefile extraction to %TEMP%, interpreter boot, a fresh fuscript connection, deletion. The 3 s probe cache cannot coalesce a 30 s cadence, the page does not check document.hidden, and the parent never checks whether Resolve's script server is up before spawning. /status, b-roll Send to Resolve and music send pay one extraction per click too.
cost: 120 spawns/hour per open music tab; at PRAC-77's measured 116 MB per extraction ~14 GB/hour of %TEMP% writes and ~120 interpreter boots and fuscript connects per hour (estimated), per editor.
evidence: Code read; import ccsync_companion.app measured at 0.16 s, so the cost is the extraction, not Python imports.
ledger: related to PRAC-77 (open) and comp-broll-music-3 (fixed the burst, not the cadence)
fix: Parent answers without a child when script_server.state() is not ready (TCP table, CR-68-safe); page skips ticks while document.hidden and backs off to 60-120 s. Keep the killable child for real Resolve calls (MED-3). Onedir (PRAC-77) removes the per-call extraction.

title: Ingest uploads spawn two rclone processes (copyto + lsjson verify) per artifact, five artifacts per clip, one at a time
what: Each artifact (poster, sprite, preview proxy, edit proxy, original) is its own rclone copyto and SFTP session, followed by an rclone lsjson session to compare size. rclone already fails a size mismatch after transfer and the server stats every file before marking it live, so lsjson is a third size check.
cost: 10 rclone spawns + 10 SSH handshakes per clip, serial: 4,000 for 400 clips, 20,000 for 2,000. At an estimated 0.5-1 s each, ~0.5-1 h or ~3-5.5 h of overhead before bytes move; three of five files per clip are sub-MB stills where the handshake is the whole cost.
evidence: Code read; per-spawn NAS cost not measured (NAS off limits).
fix: Drop the lsjson verify (rclone's own size check plus the server stat remain); send poster + sprite in one rclone copy --files-from staged under their server-allocated layout. Keep original-first ordering, copyto for server-chosen names, far-side .partial.

title: Startup walks the whole tree twice for two leftover-file sweeps that were meant to share one walk
what: sweep_stale_partials re-walks local_root with the same pruning right after fixer.walk_ccsync_tmp_files, which COMP-GUARD-1 split out so the startup sweeps share one walk. Not gated on mode, so the base rig walks P: over SMB twice.
cost: Once per start (several per day: PRAC-77 counted 24 of 55 starts as restarts on Resolve exit). 0.1 s per 50k-file local walk measured; tens of seconds of NAS metadata traffic per extra walk on the base rig (estimated).
fix: Collect Proxy/*.partial in walk_ccsync_tmp_files' loop and pass the list to sweep_stale_partials, as tmp_files is passed to the reservation sweep.

title: llama-server's log is appended for the life of the install
what: Every server start opens ~/.ccsync/state/broll_vlm_server.log in append mode; the server restarts after every gate close (editor back), and nothing truncates or rotates the file.
cost: Estimated ~20-50 KB per start plus ~1-2 KB per described clip; a few MB per thousand clips, never reclaimed.
fix: In start_server, rotate to one .1 generation when the log exceeds ~5 MB before opening it.
